questions.prompt: Fungi in a meadow break down a dead grasshopper. Which statement correctly describes what happens to its matter and its energy?

choices.text: Its matter gets reused by other living things; its energy leaves as heat.
choices.rationale: Correct. Atoms are recycled into soil and air for other organisms, while the stored energy is passed along and changed, ending up as heat that leaves the ecosystem.

choices.text: Its matter and its energy both go into the soil for plants to reuse.
choices.rationale: Energy is not recycled. Plants get their energy from sunlight, not from energy stored in the soil.

choices.text: Its matter is destroyed, but its energy is stored in the soil for later.
choices.rationale: Decomposition does not destroy matter; the atoms are rearranged and reused. And plants cannot take in energy from soil. Decomposers use the stored energy, and it ends up as heat.

choices.text: Its matter and its energy are both used up, so nothing at all gets reused.
choices.rationale: The matter is not used up. Nutrients from the grasshopper return to the soil and air and can be used again.

questions.explanation: Matter cycles: decomposers break the grasshopper's molecules into simpler substances, returning nutrients like nitrogen to the soil and carbon to the air as CO₂. questions.misconception: Decomposers recycle energy back into the soil the same way they recycle nutrients.
questions.hint: Which one can go around in a cycle, and which one gets used and spreads out as heat?
